subject: Information Theory
title: The Right to Privacy
description: A fast breakdown of The Right to Privacy for builders.

hook.text: Warren and Brandeis wrote about 'the right to be let alone' in 1890. They worried about portable cameras. Imagine today.

buildup.text: Privacy is the control of personal information flow: who knows what about you, and when.

discovery.text: Information theory quantifies privacy as limiting mutual information between your actions and an observer's knowledge.

twist.text: Digital living generates data trails that make total privacy nearly impossible. Every transaction leaves a trace.

climax.text: Privacy isn't about hiding wrongdoing. It's about maintaining information boundaries that allow freedom and dignity.

punchline.text: Privacy is control over your information. Lose it, lose autonomy.

quiz.question: How does information theory frame privacy?
options: As limiting mutual information between actions and observers
